rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate all six compounds and identify critical pairs while limiting late-elution risk. The retention window and resolutions will guide subsequent changes in gradient slope, solvent range, and temperature.

The maximum CRF is already achieved, so shorten the gradient to seek a faster fully resolved method. Keeping temperature and endpoints fixed isolates the slope effect, with the current minimum resolution of 4.20 providing substantial margin.
Shorten the gradient one grid step to test whether full resolution can be retained at a lower analysis time. Injection 2 remains a maximum-score fallback if the earliest pair drops below R = 1.5.
Test the minimum gradient duration to establish the speed–resolution boundary. The earliest pair may fall below R = 1.5; if so, the 4-minute gradient remains a fully resolved, maximum-score fallback.

Return to the shortest fully resolved gradient and raise temperature to test whether elution can be accelerated without losing the earliest pair. This isolates temperature sensitivity while retaining injection 3 as a maximum-score fallback.
Back off one temperature step from the unresolved 50 C run. The observed trend suggests 45 C may retain R ≥ 1.5 while eluting slightly faster than the fully resolved 40 C method.

Test a faster method using lower temperature to improve the critical early pair’s selectivity and a slightly reduced endpoint to soften the gradient slope. This may recover full resolution at a 2-minute gradient; injection 6 remains the fastest validated maximum-score method.

Reduce the endpoint one grid step to make the gradient shallower and lift the critical early pair above its current R of 1.49. The last peak may elute somewhat later, but the method should remain comfortably below the 10-minute scoring threshold.

Shift both endpoints upward while preserving injection 8’s gradient slope to accelerate the last peak. This tests whether the early pair retains full resolution despite the stronger starting solvent, with injection 8 as the maximum-score fallback.

Shift both endpoints upward another grid step, preserving the slope that fully resolved injection 9. This should accelerate the last peak while testing whether the earliest pair tolerates the stronger starting solvent.

Continue shifting the solvent window upward at the same gradient slope to shorten elution time. The early pair has retained R near 1.6 over the previous shifts, supporting this test at the maximum endpoint.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step while holding the endpoint at its maximum to seek earlier elution. The shallower gradient may improve separation, although the earliest pair must be checked for compression near the dead time.

Raise temperature one grid step to accelerate the last peak while using the early pair’s improved resolution margin. This tests whether the current fastest fully resolved method can remain at maximum CRF with a shorter elution time.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to test further acceleration at the current temperature. This probes whether the shallower gradient preserves early-pair resolution or whether compression near the dead time becomes limiting.

Back off the starting organic fraction to the fully resolved setting and test one higher temperature step. This establishes the thermal resolution boundary around injection 13, the fastest validated maximum-score method.

Reduce the endpoint to soften the gradient and test whether full early-pair resolution can be recovered at 35 C. This explores a warmer, shallower alternative while retaining injection 13 as the fastest validated maximum-score method.

Lower the starting organic fraction to move the critical early pair away from the pre-gradient region, while using a slightly shallower slope than injection 15. This tests whether full resolution can be recovered at 35 C without the longer final hold seen with the 0.85 endpoint.

Return to the validated 30 C temperature and lower the endpoint one step to test a nearby maximum-score method with slightly more resolution margin. Injection 13 remains the fastest fully resolved method; further heating has consistently compromised the early pair.

Back off one temperature step from injection 17 to recover early-pair resolution while keeping the first peak farther from the dead time than in injection 18. This tests a nearby fast, maximum-score alternative; injection 13 remains the fastest validated fully resolved method.

Lower temperature one step from injection 14 to test whether improved selectivity rescues the early pair at the stronger starting solvent. This completes a nearby boundary check while retaining injection 13 as the fastest validated maximum-score method.
